text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementAstronomyAre Our Hearts Strong Enough to Get to Mars?Prolonged space travel can wreak havoc on the circulatory systemJCBy Jake Currie5:30 PM CDT on October 20, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleIf humans want to have a future on Mars, we’re going to have to overcome a few hurdles first. Most of them are technological, some are logistical, but the most stubborn ones might be psychological and physiological. As it stands now, any voyage to the red planet and back will take over a year, and our muscles tend to atrophy once free from the bonds of gravity. That means our hearts are especially vulnerable to space travel. But a new study published in the journal Circulation finds this particular hurdle might not be so stubborn after all. Powered By 10 ShareNextStayHumans returning to Earth after even minimal periods in space tend to experience some adverse side effects once their feet are back on firm ground. Dizzy spells caused in part by a sudden drop in blood pressure are particularly common. Of course, going to Mars is another story.
